submission.natural_language_explanation: L17/N2593+ fires on the connector that closes a formally-named designation, above all the ' of' (and its equivalents ' van'/' de'/' la') that attaches a named legal or official instrument to its qualifier: 'the Statute of limitations' 10.7, 'the Ordinance of 1787' 12.0, 'the Decree of the committee' 10.1, 'the Act of God' 12.9, 'the Civil Rights Act of 1964' 11.0, 'the Treaty of Paris' 7.1, 'Apache License, Version 2.0' 6.6, weakening through other title-cased names (Council/Committee/Court/House/Order/Medal/League/Battle/Gulf/Revolution, 1.7-5.0) and through the 2-3 band of ' of' inside institutional and encyclopedic titles ('Court of Appeals', 'Medal of Honor', 'Forest of Dean'). It is near zero on the same connector after abstract, mass, partitive or generic-role nouns ('the idea of justice' 0.0, 'the use of force' 0.0, 'the regulation of the market' 0.04, 'the Ministry of Defence' 0.25, 'the University of Oxford' 0.7), on the lowercase common-noun use of an instrument word ('the act of God' 1.4 vs 'the Act of God' 12.9), on every other preposition after the same nouns ('the Statute on limitations' 0.9, 'the Decree by the committee' 1.8) and on bare dates with no designation ('He graduated from college in 1998' 0.4). The response reads only words already present - a year or a common noun after the same ' of' leaves it bit-identical ('the Ordinance of 1787' 11.99 = 'the Ordinance of the committee' 11.99) - while its output direction promotes the calendar months (13 of its top-13 raw-unembedding promotions, 9 of the top-10 Jacobian-lens tokens), so it writes a date bias rather than predicting a specific upcoming token, and the protocol's lookahead probe returns retrospective.

rival_explanations: The pole is a general relational-connector detector rather than a designation detector: it fires on ' of'/' de' joining any specific, concrete head noun to its qualifier, including the non-institutional cases its top examples show ('the dance of that once familiar land', 'a letter of complaint', 'the yeast of the Pharisees', 'el pie de una foto'), so it should also fire on 'the edge of the table' and 'the bark of the tree'.

The pole tracks encyclopedic names only: it fires on the connector inside a capitalised or fixed place, institution or document name ('Gulf of Mexico', 'House of Commons', 'Court of Appeals', 'Treaty of Paris'), so it should stay quiet on a legal common-noun phrase such as 'the Statute of limitations' and on the lowercase instrument word in 'an act of God'.
